author: Bobby Grayson
description: 1. It never writes a property. The skeleton's beh is the GENERATED clauses copied verbatim, so beh_eq_gen holds the moment it is written and says nothing yet; init, the bounded check and the mutant are commented stubs. A script that invented a property would produce a checker that passes by construction, which is worse than an empty one -- the whole value of the example is that a human chose a property that is actually true of the module. 2. It does not edit files under elixir/real beyond copying them in, and refuses to overwrite a copy whose bytes differ from the origin (--update is the deliberate re-land). 3. It does not add the Examples import to Leanactors.lean while the skeleton does not compile, so a bad skeleton cannot break lake build. 4. It does not touch docs/readiness.md: that is regenerated by readiness.exs, which now reads the manifest.
title: Constructs land_real.exs deliberately does NOT do, and why
